reviewNote: Drafted by Claude for faculty review from the Carson-Newman scenario. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Full stomach appendicitis in class III obesity with a documented difficult airway (grade 4 view, third attempt, SpO2 84% in 2015). The CN RSI failed first attempt case: attempt one fails by design; rescue with mask PPV and cricoid before attempt two.

asa.rationale: Class III obesity, OSA on CPAP, diabetes; urgent surgery.

decision.recommendation: proceed with an aspiration focused plan
decision.rationale: Urgent appendicitis; proceed with a difficult airway plan in place and help in the room.

redFlags.evidence: 2015 record: difficult mask, grade 4 DL, 3rd attempt with bougie, SpO2 84%; letter scanned; Mallampati IV, neck 47 cm, mouth opening 3 cm.
redFlags.implication: High chance of failed laryngoscopy and rapid desaturation.
redFlags.action: Video laryngoscope and bougie first, second provider in the room, SGA and front of neck kit ready, consider awake intubation.

redFlags.finding: Full stomach with nausea and emesis
redFlags.action: RSI with cricoid, head up, suction, no mask ventilation before the first attempt unless SpO2 falls.

redFlags.finding: OSA on CPAP with class III obesity
redFlags.implication: Fast desaturation, opioid sensitivity, postop obstruction.
redFlags.action: Ramp, 3 min preoxygenation, apneic oxygenation by nasal cannula, CPAP in PACU.
Use fentanyl or hydromorphone; multimodal analgesia.

planItems.item: Video laryngoscope plus bougie, difficult airway cart, SGA rescue, front of neck kit, call for help
RSI with cricoid and rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg (sugammadex ready)
After a failed attempt: mask PPV with cricoid until SpO2 recovers, change something before attempt two
Cefoxitin 2 g within 60 min of incision

cnRubric.title: Carson-Newman rubric: RSI, failed first attempt
